hero.eyebrow: The Elephant Coast • KwaZulu-Natal • South Africa
hero.title: Drive the wildest road in South Africa.
hero.lead: The R22 threads north from the N2 at Hluhluwe up to the Mozambique border — past the Big Five reserves, World Heritage wetlands, dive reefs and 400-year-old fish traps of Maputaland. Route22 is your guide to every stop along the way.

intro.title: One road. Every reason to come to Zululand.
intro.body: The Route22 corridor follows the R22 (the Lubombo road) as its spine, linking stretches of the N2, the P453 and the road to St Lucia, then running all the way up to Kosi Bay and round toward Pongola. Along it sits the densest concentration of wildlife, wilderness and coastline in the country — from Africa’s oldest game park to its first World Heritage Site.

st-lucia.blurb: Southern anchor of the route on the edge of iSimangaliso. Hippos and crocs in the estuary, boat cruises, and the turn-off toward Cape Vidal.

hluhluwe-imfolozi.blurb: Africa’s oldest proclaimed game reserve and the home of rhino conservation. Big Five, self-drive and guided safaris.

hluhluwe-town.blurb: Where the route meets the N2 and the R22 begins its run north. Lodges, supplies and the springboard for the reserves.

mkuze.blurb: One of the finest birding reserves in Africa, with famous hides, fig forests and pans full of game.

sodwana.blurb: World-class scuba diving on the southernmost coral reefs, deep-sea fishing and the iSimangaliso marine section.

mbazwana.blurb: Main service town on the northern R22 — fuel, shops and the crossroads for Sodwana and Lake Sibaya.

sibaya.blurb: South Africa’s largest freshwater lake, ringed by forested dunes — hippos, crocs and prolific birdlife.

rocktail.blurb: Remote beaches and turtle-nesting shores — loggerhead and leatherback turtles come ashore in summer.

tembe.blurb: Home to some of Africa’s biggest tuskers, in sand-forest wilderness on the Mozambique border.

ndumo.blurb: A birder’s holy grail on the Pongola floodplain — over 400 species and pans crowded with wildlife.

kosi-bay.blurb: Northern terminus near the border — interlinked lakes, snorkelling, and 400-year-old traditional fish traps still in use.

pongola.blurb: The western gateway — Pongolapoort Dam, tiger-fishing and Big Five reserves along the Lebombo mountains.

hluhluwe-imfolozi.desc: Big Five safaris in the oldest proclaimed game reserve in Africa, birthplace of white-rhino conservation.

isimangaliso-wetland-park.desc: South Africa’s first World Heritage Site — 21 ecosystems, from Lake St Lucia to Kosi Bay.

st-lucia.desc: The gateway town on the St Lucia estuary — hippo & croc boat cruises and the road to Cape Vidal.

sodwana-bay.desc: World-class scuba diving on the southernmost coral reefs, plus deep-sea fishing and beaches.

mkhuze-game-reserve.desc: A legendary birding reserve with famous hides, fig forests and pans full of game.

tembe-elephant-park.desc: Sand-forest wilderness sheltering some of the largest elephants left in Africa.

ndumo-game-reserve.desc: A birding paradise on the Pongola floodplain, with pans crowded with wildlife.

kosi-bay.desc: Interlinked lakes, snorkelling at the mouth, and 400-year-old traditional fish traps still in use.

lake-sibaya.desc: The largest natural freshwater lake in South Africa — hippos, crocs and prolific birdlife.

pongola.desc: The western gateway — Pongolapoort Dam, tiger-fishing and Big Five reserves under the Lebombo range.
